info.description:
The Grid is the S.I.E.R.R.A data service: public, read-only, keyless hazard,
road, weather, power and mesh-network data for the central Sierra Nevada
(Calaveras and Tuolumne counties and their corridors). Everything is under
`/api/v1`.

**Conventions that hold across the surface**

- JSON field names are camelCase. Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC strings.
  Enum values are their UPPERCASE names.
- A place is addressed by its slug (`calaveras-county`) or its namespaced id
  (`county:calaveras-county`); both resolve everywhere. List them with
  `GET /api/v1/places`.
- Events (`/api/v1/events`) are the system of record for hazards: one row per
  wildfire, evacuation zone, weather alert, earthquake, road incident, power
  outage or mesh node, each with a revision history.
- Map clients use the GeoJSON layers at
  `/api/v1/places/{place}/map/{layer}.geojson`. GeoJSON coordinates are
  `[longitude, latitude]`; the JSON RPCs use `{lat, lng}` objects.
- Severity is one scale everywhere: `INFO` < `MINOR` < `MODERATE` <
  `SEVERE` < `EXTREME` (rank 0-4).
- **Fail loud.** Every layer and summary domain reports source health as
  `OK`, `STALE` (serving the last good data, see `lastSourceUpdate`) or
  `UNAVAILABLE` (nothing to show; the state is UNKNOWN, not clear). Never
  render an UNAVAILABLE layer or a `null` count as "all clear".
- Evacuation and other life-safety text is reference only. Show it verbatim
  and link the authoritative source (`sourceUrl`).

**Caching.** Read responses carry `Cache-Control: public, max-age=30`
(GeoJSON layers and mesh links: 60). The RPCs marked with a `304` response
honour `If-None-Match`; send back the `ETag` you received.

**Errors.** Every JSON route, generated or hand-built, answers errors as
`{code, codeName, message, details}` (`rpcStatus`) with the HTTP status
mapped from the gRPC code. Branch on `codeName`. During a deploy handoff
any route can briefly answer `503` with a plain-text body and
`Retry-After: 1`.

**CORS** is open (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) for GET only. The two
POST routes (`/api/v1/ingest/{stream}`, `/mcp`) are not callable
cross-origin from a browser.

The JSON RPCs also accept proto field names for query parameters
(`page_token` as well as `pageToken`).

The proto-defined read surface: events and their history, places, place
summaries, conditions, sources, cameras, scanners and mesh telemetry.

RFC 7946 GeoJSON, one FeatureCollection per place and layer, ready to hand
to MapLibre GL, Leaflet or OpenLayers. Hand-built (proto models geometry
poorly), so these routes are described here rather than generated.

The MeshCore community mesh: node presence is the `mesh_node` map layer
and `layer=MESH` events; the relay topology is `/api/v1/mesh/links` and
the `mesh_link` map layer; per-node history is `GetMeshTelemetry`.

get.description: OpenAPI 3.0, built from grid.proto plus a hand-written overlay. `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`.

get.summary:
ListCameras returns Caltrans traffic cameras (CCTV) in or near the
coverage areas: a snapshot image and, where Caltrans publishes one, an HLS
stream per camera. Links only — the images and streams are served by
Caltrans, never proxied. ?place narrows the set to cameras within the same
radius of that place, nearest first. Cameras are reference views, not
events: nothing here is a hazard and an empty list means no camera nearby.

GetConditions returns current, non-event state: per-location weather and
the region's fire-weather classification, optionally scoped to a place.
(Weather alerts are events; road conditions are the road_segment /
chain_control GeoJSON layers.)

ListEvents returns store-backed events filtered by place, layer, status,
severity_min, and since, with keyset pagination.
GetEvent returns the current revision of one event by id.
GetEventHistory returns one event's revisions, newest first, paginated.
ListHistory returns revisions across events over a [from, to) window.

post.description:
The only write endpoint, for operator-run monitors (see
docs/mesh-reporter-guide.md). Each reporter is granted specific streams.
A report is validated and queued (202), not stored synchronously: the
ingest scheduler merges it on its next tick, and no request writes an
event directly.

Checks run in this order and nothing in the body is read before the
caller is known: bearer token (401) -> stream exists (404) -> reporter
granted the stream (403) -> rate limit (429) -> body size (413) ->
payload (400). A malformed envelope rejects the whole report; a bad
entry is skipped and named in `warnings`.

**Limits.** One accepted report per reporter per stream every 15
seconds by default (measured from the last ACCEPTED report, so rejected
retries never lock you out); 1 MiB body; 1000 entries. Retries are
safe: entries are keyed by node or line.

**Preflight.** `?preflight=true` checks the token and grant only and
answers 204, recording nothing (no rate-limit or health effect). Use it
before expensive work such as placing a phone call.

Errors use the same `rpcStatus` envelope as every other route. Any
method other than POST answers `405` with `Allow: POST` (body code 12,
`UNIMPLEMENTED`).

Not callable from a browser cross-origin (CORS allows GET only). The
route is mounted only when the deployment configures reporters.

get.description:
Every undirected relay link observed within `window`, mesh-wide (not
place-scoped: a mesh spans places). Nodes are identified by public key;
to draw a link, join `a` and `b` to `properties.mesh.publicKey` on the
`mesh_node` map layer (or `mesh.publicKey` on `layer=MESH` events) for
coordinates. For a place-scoped, ready-to-draw version use the
`mesh_link` map layer. Weight edges by `daysActive`, fade by `lastSeen`.

`Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` and a weak `ETag` (`W/"…"`) that
excludes `generatedAt`: `If-None-Match` revalidates to `304` until the
links change.
get.summary: The MeshCore relay topology, as an edge list

get.description:
The event carries a node's LATEST reading; this carries every reading, and
only the second can be graphed. Per node by design: this is one node's
chart, and a cross-node dump would be a different (and far larger) product.

parameters.description: the node's full public key, hex
parameters.name: node

get.summary:
GetMeshTelemetry returns ONE node's archived operator-monitor samples — the
series behind a battery, temperature or airtime chart.
ListPlaces returns the place directory filtered by kind and a name query.
GetPlace returns one place by slug or namespaced id.

get.description:
An RFC 7946 FeatureCollection of one layer's features within a place.
Coordinates are `[longitude, latitude]`. Check `metadata.sourceStatus`
before drawing: UNAVAILABLE means unknown (empty `features`), STALE
means last-good data.

| layer | features | backed by |
|---|---|---|
| `road_incident` | Points: CHP incidents (category `incident`) and Caltrans planned lane closures (`closure`, SCHEDULED until set up) | events |
| `chain_control` | Points: active R1/R2/R3 checkpoints and seasonal pass closures | live Caltrans |
| `road_segment` | LineStrings: configured routes with travel time; `status` OPEN/CLOSED/RESTRICTED/MAINTENANCE | live Google Routes + Caltrans |
| `message_sign` | Points: Caltrans message signs and their text; always INFO | live Caltrans |
| `weather_alert` | null geometry: NWS zone watches/warnings/advisories | events |
| `fire_weather` | one null-geometry region banner (`fw:region`) plus forecast Points | live NWS |
| `earthquake` | Points | events (USGS) |
| `wildfire` | Points or (Multi)Polygon perimeters | events (CAL FIRE, FIRIS) |
| `evacuation` | (Multi)Polygon zones; `status` is the level | events (Cal OES) |
| `power` | Polygons/Points: PG&E outages (`unplanned`/`planned`) and PSPS (`psps`) | events |
| `mesh_node` | Points: MeshCore nodes in the place; always INFO | events |
| `mesh_link` | LineString relay links touching the place plus the MESH_NODE Points at both ends (neighbours outside the place have `mesh.inRegion: false`); honours `window` | derived |
| `camera` | Points: Caltrans CCTV cameras near the place, nearest first; always INFO | live Caltrans |

Event-backed layers carry only ACTIVE and SCHEDULED features, and each
feature `id` is an event id usable with `/api/v1/events/{id}`. The
`.geojson` suffix is optional (`/map/wildfire` is the same resource).

**Caching.** `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` and a weak `ETag`
(`W/"…"`) over the layer's content, excluding `metadata.generatedAt`.
Revalidate with `If-None-Match`: the answer is `304` until the
features, `sourceStatus`, `lastSourceUpdate` or `attribution` change,
so polling a quiet layer costs no body.

GetPlaceSummary is the one-call place rollup: mode, a cross-layer severity
summary, per-domain status, top events, the evacuation invariant, and a
source-health sidecar. (3-segment path; no collision with GetPlace.)

ResolvePlace maps a lat/lng or address to the containing places,

post.description:
A read-only MCP server (protocol revision `2025-06-18`, server name
`sierra-grid`) for LLM agents. Stateless request/response: POST one
JSON-RPC message, get one JSON response (no SSE stream, no session id).
A notification (no `id`) is answered `202` with no body. Any other HTTP
method is `405`. Tools call this same `/api/v1` surface in-process and
every result carries a reference-only disclaimer.

Tools (`tools/list` for their input schemas):
- `grid_situation`: what is happening at a place, address or lat,lng
  (mode, per-domain status, top headlines). Start here.
- `grid_events`: list events, filtered by location, layer, severity,
  status and time.
- `grid_event`: one event in full, by id.
- `grid_conditions`: current weather and fire-weather state.
- `grid_resolve`: address or lat,lng to the places containing it.
- `grid_places`: the place directory.
- `grid_sources`: feed health.
- `grid_history`: revisions over a time range.

Resource `grid://reference` (the API reference, Markdown); prompt
`hazard_briefing(location)`.

Not callable from a browser cross-origin (CORS allows GET only).

200.description: A JSON-RPC response (success or JSON-RPC error; the HTTP status is 200 either way).

202.description: The message was a notification. No body.

post.summary: Model Context Protocol (JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP)

ETag.description:
Validator for conditional GET, weak (`W/"…"`) or strong. Send it back
verbatim as `If-None-Match` to get a `304 Not Modified` when nothing
changed.

IfNoneMatch.description: An `ETag` from an earlier response, for a `304` revalidation.
IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match

MeshWindow.description:
Recency window for relay links: a positive Go duration. The documented
choices are `24h`, `72h` (the default), `168h` and `720h`; any positive
duration works (`90m`), and values above `9600h` (400 days) are
clamped. Anything else (`abc`, `0`, `-1h`) is a `400
INVALID_ARGUMENT`. `/api/v1/mesh/links` echoes the applied window in
`window`.
MeshWindow.name: window

Place.description:
A place slug (`calaveras-county`, `ebbetts-pass`, `hwy4-murphys-arnold`)
or namespaced id (`county:calaveras-county`). Slugs are globally unique.
`GET /api/v1/places` lists them; `GET /api/v1/places:resolve` maps an
address or lat/lng to the places containing it.
Place.name: place

text/plain.example: service is handing over to a new instance; retry

HandoffUnavailable.description:
The server is handing over to a new instance during a deploy. Retry after
`Retry-After` seconds. Plain text, not JSON.

Internal.description: Server-side failure. The real error is logged, never sent.

InvalidArgument.description: A malformed parameter (bad `pageToken`, unknown enum, bad timestamp).

value.message: invalid window "abc": want a positive duration such as 72h

InvalidWindow.description: `window` is not a positive Go duration (`abc`, `0`, `-1h`).

NotFound.description: The named place, event or other resource does not exist.

NotModified.description:
The `If-None-Match` validator still matches; reuse your cached body.
No body.

line_id.description: A configured line id (grid.burn.lines); unknown ids are warnings.

observed_at.description: When the line was called. Required; future stamps are clamped.

BurnLineReport.description:
`burn.line` (schema_version 1): readings of the county burn-day phone
recordings, sent as ONE batched report per run (the per-reporter rate
limit would 429 a second push). Each reading is staged durably.

IngestAccepted.description: The 202 body. Validated and queued, not yet stored; it lands on the next ingest cycle (about a minute).

accepted.description: mesh.repeater: nodes accepted. mesh.packet: ADVERTs applied (not packets received). burn.line: readings staged.

reporterId.description: The reporter the token belongs to.

warnings.description: Entries skipped without failing the report (bad id, duplicate, unknown line, bad signature). Fix your output if present. mesh.packet lists at most 25, then a count.

JsonRpcRequest.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 request. Omit `id` for a notification (answered 202, no body).

id.description: Request id (string or number), echoed in the response.

error.description: Present on failure. -32700 parse error, -32601 method not found, -32602 invalid params, -32603 internal error.

id.description: The request's id; null when the request could not be parsed.

MapCameraProps.description: camera block - a Caltrans CCTV camera, same data as GET /api/v1/cameras?place=. Load the image and stream directly from Caltrans; they are not proxied.

distanceMeters.description: Distance from the requested place; 0 = inside it.

imageRefreshMinutes.description: How often Caltrans refreshes the snapshot. Absent = not reported.

streamUrl.description: HLS .m3u8 live stream. Absent = image only.

MapChainControlProps.description: chain_control block. Severity follows the level (R1 MINOR, R2 MODERATE, R3 SEVERE); a seasonal pass closure (`category` closed) is MINOR.

MapClosureProps.description:
Set on Caltrans planned lane closures (category `closure`) only. One
feature per work window. `plannedEnd` is an estimate crews overrun: an
ACTIVE closure past it is still on the road until Caltrans records it
picked up.

lanesClosed.description: Caltrans's lane list, verbatim., example: "1, 2, LShoulder, RShoulder"

setUpAt.description: When the crew reported the closure set up. Absent while SCHEDULED.

MapEvacuationProps.description: evacuation block (Cal OES / Genasys zones). Life-safety; reference only, link `source.url`.

MapFeatureCollection.description:
An RFC 7946 FeatureCollection for one place and one layer. `metadata` is
an RFC 7946 §6.1 foreign member that map libraries ignore; read it for
source health and attribution before drawing.

features.description: Possibly empty. Empty with `sourceStatus` OK means confirmed-empty; empty with UNAVAILABLE means unknown.

MapFeatureProperties.description:
The envelope shared by every feature of every layer, plus exactly one
per-kind block named after the layer (`incident`, `road`,
`chainControl`, `messageSign`, `weather`, `fireWeather`, `earthquake`,
`wildfire`, `evacuation`, `power`, `mesh`, `meshLink`, `camera`).
Optional members are omitted, never `""` or `0`, when they have no value.

areaLabel.description: Where, in words ("SR 4 at Country Club Drive", "Murphys, CA").

description.description:
Longer text. road_incident: the readable narrative (AI-enhanced for
CHP, composed from Caltrans fields for closures). evacuation: Cal OES
public info, verbatim, never paraphrase. weather_alert: the NWS text,
verbatim. road_segment: why a road is not OPEN.

effective.description: When it began or takes effect (a SCHEDULED feature's start).

expires.description: Upstream expiry (weather alerts, fire-weather products). Not set from PG&E restoration estimates.

headline.description: One-line label for a popup or list row.

id.description:
Stable feature id. On event-backed layers it IS the event id, so
`GET /api/v1/events/{id}` returns the full record and its history
(`wildfire`, `evacuation`, `weather_alert`, `earthquake`,
`road_incident`, `power`, `mesh_node`). Condition layers use their
own ids (`road:…`, `cc:…`, `cms:…`, `fw:…`, `mesh_link:…`, `d10-…`).

kind.description: Human label for the feature type.

layer.description:
UPPERCASE layer of THIS feature. Usually the URL layer upper-cased,
except that the `mesh_link` layer mixes `MESH_LINK` edges and
`MESH_NODE` points. Only some values equal an Event `layer` enum
(`v1Layer`): WILDFIRE, EVACUATION, WEATHER_ALERT, EARTHQUAKE,
ROAD_INCIDENT and POWER do. MESH_NODE is the Event layer `MESH`.
ROAD_SEGMENT, CHAIN_CONTROL, MESSAGE_SIGN, MESH_LINK and CAMERA are
map-only. FIRE_WEATHER exists in the enum but these features are
conditions, not events.

severity.description:
Unified severity. `message_sign`, `camera`, `mesh_node`, `mesh_link`
and fire-weather forecast points are always `INFO` (context, not
hazards). Most power outages are INFO too: the median outage affects
one customer.

severityRank.description: Numeric severity for sorting and styling: INFO 0, MINOR 1, MODERATE 2, SEVERE 3, EXTREME 4.

status.description:
Meaning depends on the layer, and it is NOT always the Event
`EventStatus`:
- wildfire, weather_alert, earthquake, road_incident, power,
  mesh_node: the lifecycle `ACTIVE` or `SCHEDULED` (an advance watch,
  a planned closure window not yet set up, a planned shutoff). Map
  layers never carry RESOLVED or EXPIRED features; those are in
  `/api/v1/history`.
- evacuation: the evacuation LEVEL `ORDER` | `WARNING` | `ADVISORY` |
  `SHELTER_IN_PLACE`.
- road_segment: the road status `OPEN` | `CLOSED` | `RESTRICTED` |
  `MAINTENANCE` (absent until the road has been measured).
- absent on chain_control, message_sign, fire_weather, camera and
  mesh_link edges.

summary.description: AI-written plain-language summary (same as Event.summary). Absent when the event has none; fall back to `description`.

summaryEnhanced.description: Present with `summary` when a model wrote it, so a UI can label it as machine-written.

updatedAt.description: Last content revision. For mesh nodes this is NOT liveness; use mesh.lastHeardAt / lastRelayedAt.

MapFeatureSource.description: The upstream feed this feature came from. Render `attribution` with the feature.

id.description: Source registry id (see GET /api/v1/sources): chp, caltrans, google, nws, usgs, calfire, firis, caloes, pge, psps, meshcore.

url.description: Deep link to the upstream record or viewer, when there is one.

MapFireWeatherProps.description:
fire_weather block. The region banner (id `fw:region`, null geometry)
carries the ISSUED `state`; only NWS products set it (Fire Weather Watch
-> elevated, Red Flag Warning -> red-flag). Forecast points (id
`fw:forecast:<location>`) carry `forecast` instead, are always INFO and
never imply a warning.

sourceEvent.description: The NWS product behind the state, e.g. Red Flag Warning.

MapGeometry.description:
An RFC 7946 geometry, or `null` for a feature with no location (NWS zone
alerts and the fire-weather region banner): render those as a banner
or list row, not a shape.

A position is `[longitude, latitude]`, longitude FIRST (RFC 7946
§3.1.1), the reverse of the `{lat, lng}` objects on the JSON RPCs.
Store-derived positions are trimmed to 5 decimals (~1 m).

Which types appear: Point (most layers: incidents, signs, cameras,
chain controls, quakes, mesh nodes, forecast points, unmapped fires);
LineString (road_segment routes, mesh_link edges); Polygon or
MultiPolygon (power outage areas, evacuation zones, fire perimeters).
Geometry passed through from an upstream ArcGIS feed may be any RFC 7946
type except GeometryCollection.

logNumber.description: CHP log number, or the Caltrans closure id.

MapLayerMetadata.description: Provenance and freshness of the whole layer.

area.description: Slug of the requested place (even when it was requested by id).

attribution.description: Credit line to render with the layer whenever it is drawn. Parts are joined with " · ".

generatedAt.description: When this body was rendered. Not part of the ETag.

lastSourceUpdate.description: Last successful upstream fetch. Present only when `sourceStatus` is not OK and a success is on record.

layer.description: The lowercase layer slug from the URL (not the UPPERCASE `properties.layer`).

schemaVersion.description: Envelope schema version; bumps only on a breaking envelope change.

sourceStatus.description:
Health of the feeds behind this layer, the fail-loud contract:
`OK` - current and complete. `STALE` - upstream is failing (or one
of two feeds is); these features are the last good data, as of
`lastSourceUpdate`. Show them with a caveat. `UNAVAILABLE` - nothing
trustworthy to show; `features` is always empty and the layer's
state is UNKNOWN. Never render it as "no hazards".

sourceUrl.description: The authoritative viewer for the layer, where one exists. Always set on `evacuation` (Genasys Protect), in every state.

MapMeshAdminProps.description: The last sample an operator monitor read off the node itself. Gauges the device did not report are absent, never 0.

MapMeshLinkProps.description: mesh_link edge block - one undirected relay link between two located nodes. Weight by `daysActive`/`observations`, fade by `lastSeen`.

a.description: Public key of one end (a < b).

b.description: Public key of the other end.

bestSnr.description: Peak SNR of an advert over the link. Absent when 0.

daysActive.description: Distinct days the link was observed.

observations.description: Packets seen traversing the link in the window.

MapMeshProps.description:
mesh_node block (MeshCore node presence; also on the MESH_NODE points of
the mesh_link layer). Signal readings are absent when no bridge heard the
node; a present 0 is a reading. A node's freshness is the later of
`lastHeardAt` and `lastRelayedAt`, never the feature's `updatedAt`.

gateways.description: Public keys of the observers that heard the node.

hopCount.description: Hops on the last heard path. 0 = heard direct.

inRegion.description: mesh_link layer only: true = inside the requested place, false = a neighbour outside it, included because it links in.

lastHeardAt.description: When the node's own signed advert last reached the Grid.

lastRelayedAt.description: When a packet this node relayed last reached the Grid.

publicKey.description: 64-hex Ed25519 public key; joins to MeshLink a/b.

reachability.description: An operator monitor's verdict on the node's admin interface. Absent when no monitor watches it.

MapMessageSignProps.description: message_sign block - what a Caltrans changeable message sign is showing, verbatim. Context, not a hazard.

pages.description: One or two pages of exactly three lines; a blank line is "". Absent when the sign is blank or unreadable.

MapPowerProps.description:
power block, both PG&E feeds. `category` unplanned|planned sets the
outage fields; `psps` (Public Safety Power Shutoff) sets the PSPS fields.
`estimatedRestoration`, `deEnergizationEnd` and `allClear` are PG&E
ESTIMATES that are routinely overrun; label them as estimates.

allClear.description: PG&E's PLANNED all-clear, not proof the shutoff ended.

cause.description: Raw PG&E cause code, often blank.

medicalBaselineAffected.description: Customers whose medical equipment depends on grid power.

MapRoadProps.description: road_segment block (Google Routes travel time over a configured route). The numbers are absent, not 0, until the route has been measured.

delayMinutes.description: Minutes over free-flow. 0 is a real reading.

MapWeatherProps.description: weather_alert block. The NWS CAP fields are verbatim; `nwsSeverity` is NWS's own scale, distinct from the unified `severity`.

MapWildfireProps.description: wildfire block (CAL FIRE incidents and FIRIS perimeters).

hasPerimeter.description: True when the geometry is a mapped perimeter rather than a point.

MeshLink.description: One undirected relay link. Every member is always present.

a.description: Public key (64 hex) of one end; a < b.

b.description: Public key of the other end.

bestSnr.description: Peak SNR (dB) of an advert seen traversing it; 0 when none was measured.

daysActive.description: Distinct days observed; a reliability weight.

observations.description: Packets seen traversing the link in the window.

MeshPacket.description: One reception. Extra bridge fields are accepted and ignored.

RSSI.description: Reception RSSI in dBm (number or numeric string).

SNR.description: Reception SNR in dB (number or numeric string).

origin_id.description: Receiving radio's public key, if different from `observer`.

packet_type.description: MeshCore payload type; only 4 (ADVERT) updates a node.

raw.description: The full over-the-air frame as hex (header, path, payload), or a meshcore://<hex> link.

timestamp.description: Ignored; the server stamps its own receive time.

MeshPacketReport.description:
`mesh.packet` (schema_version 1): raw MeshCore frames a companion radio
heard, in the per-packet envelope the MQTT bridges publish. ADVERTs
(packet_type 4) update a node after its Ed25519 signature verifies;
other flood-routed packets credit relays. Answers 400 when MeshCore
ingest is off on the server.

observer.description: Public key (or 4+ byte prefix) of the receiving radio. Defaults to the reporter id.

id.description: Node public key or a prefix of it (8-64 hex). A bad id is a warning; the rest of the report still lands.

last_attempt.description: Unix seconds of the monitor's last attempt on this node.

last_success.description: Unix seconds of the last successful read; null if never. Reachability is derived from its age.

online.description: Accepted and logged, but not used; reachability comes from last_success.

MeshRepeaterReport.description:
`mesh.repeater` (schema_version 1): an operator monitor's COMPLETE
current set of MeshCore repeaters it logged into. A report replaces the
reporter's previous set; a node left out is no longer monitored. Request
bodies are snake_case. Unknown fields are ignored. Unread values are
`null`, never `0`.

generated_at.description: When the report was built. Clamped to the server's clock.

rpcStatus.description:
The error body of every JSON route: the RPCs (gRPC-Gateway rendering of
google.rpc.Status) and the hand-built GeoJSON, mesh-links and ingest
routes alike. Served with the HTTP status mapped from `code`
(3 INVALID_ARGUMENT -> 400, 5 NOT_FOUND -> 404, 13 INTERNAL -> 500,
14 UNAVAILABLE -> 503, ...). All four members are always present.

codeName.description:
Canonical gRPC code name for `code`, e.g. `NOT_FOUND`,
`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `INTERNAL`. Branch on this rather than the
message.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Not stable; do not parse.

v1BurnDay.title:
- BURN_DAY_UNKNOWN: not reached, or the reading was unusable/stale
 - BURN_DAY_YES: permissive burn day — burning allowed
 - BURN_DAY_NO: no-burn day — burning prohibited
 - BURN_DAY_MARGINAL: restricted/partial (the line's "orange")

v1BurnLineReading.description: BurnLineReading is one recorded phone line's answer for today.

phone.title: the number a resident can call

v1BurnObservation.description:
BurnObservation is the volatile half of a burn status reading. It is grouped
into its own sub-message so store.ContentHash can zero the whole field.

This is load-bearing, not tidiness. The county line's message NAMES THE DATE
("Today, September 10th, is a burn day in Calaveras County"), so the text
differs every single day even when the answer has not changed. Hashed, it
would mint a revision daily and bury the handful of real transitions — the
only thing this layer exists to record — in 365 rows of noise a year.

confidence.description:
The transcription model's own confidence, 0-100. Surfaced rather than
thresholded: this is an LLM reading of phone audio, and a consumer deserves
to see when the read was shaky.

observedAt.title: when this line was last called

v1BurnPermission.title:
- BURN_PERMISSION_UNKNOWN: at least one facet unknown — assume nothing
 - BURN_PERMISSION_ALLOWED: both facets permit burning today
 - BURN_PERMISSION_PROHIBITED: at least one facet prohibits it

v1BurnStatusDetail.description:
Residential/outdoor burning status for one county (Layer_BURN_STATUS).

TWO INDEPENDENT AUTHORITIES gate a legal burn, and BOTH must permit it:

 1. `burn_day` — the county air district's permissive-burn-day call, decided
    daily from meteorology and air quality. Flips weekly in winter/spring.
 2. `calfire_status` — CAL FIRE's seasonal suspension of residential burn
    permits on State Responsibility Area land. Moves about twice a year.

They are carried separately, never merged into one upstream value, because
they fail independently: the county line can be unreachable while CAL FIRE's
page is fine, and vice versa. `permission` is the only derived answer, and it
is deliberately pessimistic (see below).

This is AMBIENT state, not a hazard: the event exists for a county at all
times and is excluded from the summary hazard rollup, exactly like mesh-node
presence. Its VALUE is the revision history — "when did it change" is the
question this layer answers.

burnLines.description:
--- county facet (source `burnline`) ---
Every recorded line that speaks for this county, each with its own reading.

Repeated rather than one phone number because the line-to-county mapping is
not 1:1 in EITHER direction: a county can have more than one relevant
recording, and one air-district line routinely covers several counties.
`burn_day` above is these lines merged, taking the most restrictive.

A line with no usable reading still appears here, with burn_day UNKNOWN and
its phone populated — that is the honest thing to show, and it is what lets
a consumer say "we could not read it, here is the number".

calfireEffective.description:
--- CAL FIRE facet (source `calfire-burn`) ---
When the suspension took effect. The county phone line only ever says
"until further notice"; this date exists nowhere else we read.

calfireObservedAt.description:
When the CAL FIRE page was last read successfully. EXCLUDED from the content
hash (store.ContentHash), like the per-line observations: it moves every
tick and would otherwise mint a revision every tick.

It exists because the envelope's own observed_at cannot answer this. When
the CAL FIRE scrape fails, that facet is carried forward from the stored
event while observed_at still advances (we did poll) — so this is the only
way a consumer can see the suspension value is not freshly confirmed.

v1CalfireBurnStatus.title:
- CALFIRE_BURNING_SUSPENDED: permits suspended; no residential burning
 - CALFIRE_PERMIT_REQUIRED: burning allowed with a valid permit
 - CALFIRE_NO_PERMIT_REQUIRED: off-season; no permit needed

v1Camera.description:
Camera is one Caltrans CCTV camera. Every listed camera is in service and has
an image; an out-of-service camera is dropped, not flagged.

description.title: Caltrans's note on the view, e.g. "Looking South"; usually empty

distanceMeters.description:
Metres from the requested place — or, without ?place, from the nearest
coverage area. 0 means inside it.

id.title: "d10-172": Caltrans district + the portal's camera index

imageRefreshMinutes.title: how often Caltrans replaces the snapshot; 0 = not reported

imageUrl.title: the current snapshot JPEG on cwwp2.dot.ca.gov

streamUrl.title: HLS playlist (.m3u8); empty for an image-only camera

lastSourceUpdate.description: When the served list was fetched. Unset when source_status is OK.

sourceStatus.description:
OK | STALE | UNAVAILABLE — the camera LIST's health, the same honesty
field the map layers carry. STALE: served from an older fetch (or a
configured district is missing). UNAVAILABLE: no list has been fetched
yet, or no camera districts are configured.

v1Enhancement.description:
AI-enhancement provenance so clients can badge AI-summarized text
(spec §3.1: translate, never assert; originals preserved in description).

request.description:
Transparency: the exact model input and output, so a client can show what
was sent and what came back. `request` is the incident-specific user prompt
(the static system prompt is not included); `response` is the raw structured
JSON the model returned. Excluded from the event content hash.

v1EventStatus.title:
- SCHEDULED: planned PSPS, forecast closures
 - RESOLVED: upstream confirmed over
 - EXPIRED: aged out per-source policy; upstream went quiet

v1FireWeatherDetail.description:
fire_weather is condition-backed (a live projection, not an event); this
message exists for the spec §3 oneof shape.

v1ForecastPeriod.description:
ForecastPeriod is one hourly step of a location's fire-weather forecast (NWS
gridpoint). Absent numeric fields serialize as 0, like WeatherConditions.

v1LaneClosureDetail.description:
One Caltrans planned lane-closure WINDOW, read from the CWWP2 data portal.
Every field is upstream data; none of it is AI-generated.

The unit is the window because Caltrans has no other one. A multi-day job is
one row per day, and neither closure_id nor log_number identifies a job:
closure_id is a route-level project id, and one log number can cover
windows at different places on different days, or be re-issued daily at
the same place. window_id is the only unique key.

The planned window is an estimate that crews overrun, so planned_end is NOT
mapped onto the envelope `expires` (the same rule as PG&E's restoration
estimate). A set-up closure stays ACTIVE until the crew radios it picked up,
or until planned_end plus a configured overrun grace (12h by default) passes
with no pickup call, when it is presumed picked up and RESOLVED. Indefinite
windows have no such bound.

district.title: Caltrans district whose feed listed it

endLocation.title: equals begin_location for a closure at one spot

setUpAt.title: the 10-97 call: crew on scene, closure in place

totalLanes.title: lanes at the site; 0 when not reported

v1Layer.title: - POWER: condition-backed layers (ROAD_SEGMENT, CHAIN_CONTROL) are projections, not events

v1MeshAdminTelemetry.description:
MeshAdminTelemetry is one sample read off a node's own admin interface by an
operator-run monitor and pushed to POST /api/v1/ingest/mesh.repeater. It is
the node's self-reported view, which is why it duplicates rather than
overwrites the gateway-reported snr/rssi above: those are what a distant
listener heard, these are what the node itself measured.

Gauges are wrapper types, not bare scalars, so "the monitor could not read
this" (null) stays distinguishable from a real zero — a 0% battery and an
unknown battery must never render alike. Same reasoning as the place summary's
activeEvacuations. Counters are lifetime-since-boot and plain: a node that has
sent nothing genuinely has sent zero.

batteryPercentSource.description:
"measured" | "estimated" — an estimate derived from voltage is not a reading,
and a UI that shows 97% should be able to say which it is.

lastAttemptAt.title: monitor's last attempt, successful or not

lastSuccessAt.title: monitor's last successful read of THIS node

reportedAt.title: when the monitor generated the report

v1MeshDetail.description:
MeshCore mesh-node presence (Layer_MESH). One event per node, keyed by
its Ed25519 public key. Stable identity + advertised location live here (and
mint a revision on change); the per-packet signal metrics live in the nested
MeshTelemetry, which the store's ContentHash zeroes — so the firehose of
adverts refreshes liveness (last_seen_at) without ever writing a revision.

publicKey.title: full Ed25519 public key, hex (also the Event.id native part)

v1MeshReachability.description:
MeshReachability is an operator monitor's verdict on a node's admin interface.

 - MESH_REACHABILITY_UNSPECIFIED: no monitor watches this node
 - REACHABLE: a monitor reached it within the window
 - UNREACHABLE: a monitor has been failing past the window

v1MeshTelemetry.description:
MeshTelemetry is the volatile, per-advert signal state. It is deliberately
grouped into one sub-message so store.ContentHash can zero the whole field:
none of it mints a revision.

gateways.title: origin ids of the gateways/brokers that heard it

hopCount.title: path length of the last-heard advert

lastAdvertAt.title: sender-stamped time of the last advert

lastHeardAt.description:
When WE last received one of this node's own adverts (our clock, not the
node's: compare last_advert_at). This is the answer to "when did the node
last speak". The event's observed_at is NOT: it moves only when something
hashed changes (identity, position, reachability), so a node advertising
the same thing every day kept an observed_at days old.

Read-time only. Filled from the store's mesh_activity table when the event
is served and never written into the event blob, so it mints no revision
and costs no blob rewrite. Null when no advert has been received since
activity tracking began.

lastRelayedAt.description:
When we last received a packet that this node had RELAYED: its key's hash
appeared as a hop in the path of a FLOOD-routed packet of any type
(messages, acks, path returns, adverts). A backbone repeater adverts every
day or two but relays constantly, so this, not last_heard_at, is what says
a repeater is up right now.

Two limits, both deliberate. A hop is credited only when exactly one
relay-capable node fits it: a 2- or 3-byte hash by unique prefix, a 1-byte
hash only as the one known neighbour of the next hop along (the observer
heard the last hop directly) that carries the byte. A node seen only on
1-byte paths beside nodes it has never been linked to gets no relay time.
And direct-routed packets never count: their path is the route still to be
travelled, not the one travelled, so a hop there may never have heard the
packet. A relay also keeps an already-known node PRESENT (ACTIVE) for
grid.meshcore.relayPresence after it, the way an advert does; it never
creates a node or changes its identity or position. Read-time only, like
last_heard_at; null when no relay has been attributed.

snr.description:
Wrapper types, not bare scalars, for the reason the admin gauges below are:
under the gateway's EmitUnpopulated marshaler an unset scalar is published
as 0, and here that 0 is a claim. A node an operator's monitor reports but
no MQTT bridge has ever heard was going out as `snr: 0, rssi: 0,
hopCount: 0` — a reading of 0 dB, heard DIRECT, for a node the mesh has not
heard at all (observed live 2026-09-15 on three of nine monitored
repeaters). hop_count makes it sharpest: 0 hops is a real and meaningful
reading, so it cannot double as "unknown".

Absent now means absent: these are null unless an MQTT bridge reported the
advert they came from, which `last_advert_at` also marks.

last SNR (dB), gateway-reported

v1MeshTelemetryArchive.description:
MeshTelemetryArchive is one node's samples over a window, with what a chart
needs in order not to lie about them.

cadenceSeconds.description:
The observed MEDIAN gap between samples, so a client knows which gaps are
abnormal enough to break a line on. Null with fewer than two samples: one
point has no cadence. Median, not mean — one multi-hour outage in a day of
15-minute reports drags a mean past anything the feed does.

reboots.description:
Sample times where the node's uptime went BACKWARDS. Every lifetime counter
restarts there, so a line drawn across one plunges to zero and climbs back —
a graph of our arithmetic rather than of the mesh. Also a fact worth seeing.

truncated.description:
The window held more samples than one response carries. Stated, never
silent: a chart that ends early because the server stopped talking must not
look like a chart of a node that stopped.

v1MeshTelemetrySample.description:
MeshTelemetrySample is one archived report.

The reading is MeshAdminTelemetry itself — the same message the event carries,
not a flattened copy of its 23 fields. One definition means the archive and
the live event cannot describe the same reading differently, and the gauges
keep their wrapper types, so an unread battery stays null here too.

receivedAt.title: when the Grid first held it

id.title: "area:ebbetts-pass" — existing area ids preserved under a kind

v1PlaceKind.title: - AREA: existing configured areas; org footprints live here too

v1PlaceSummary.description:
PlaceSummary is the one-call place rollup (the former hand-built summary,
now proto so it is camelCase like the rest of the surface). active_evacuations
is a wrapper so it can serialize as an explicit JSON null: null when the
evacuation source is UNAVAILABLE (unknown — render "check Genasys"), 0 when
confirmed-empty (OK/STALE with no active zones), N when active. An error must
never become a 0.

v1PowerDetail.description:
PG&E electric outages and Public Safety Power Shutoffs (Layer_POWER). One
message covers both, because they are the same thing to a reader — the power
is out, or is about to be — and they differ only in which block is populated:
an unplanned/planned outage carries outage_id + crew_status, a PSPS carries
the event/stage/de-energization window. The envelope `category`
(unplanned|planned|psps) says which.

allClear.description:
PG&E's all-clear time for the window. This is a PLANNED time, not proof the
shutoff ended: it is populated on rows still at stage `Watch`, where it
simply mirrors de_energization_end. It therefore MUST NOT drive lifecycle —
resolving an event on it would clear a shutoff that is still on, which is
the worst thing this layer could do. It is carried so a client can show the
expected all-clear alongside the other estimates.

customersAffected.title: EST_CUSTOMERS (statewide median is 1 — see the severity mapping)

estimatedRestoration.description:
Estimated time of restoration. This is an ESTIMATE and is routinely wrong
(observed: an ETOR of 19:00Z on an outage still active at 22:00Z), so it is
deliberately NOT mapped onto the envelope `expires`: `expires` is what
shouldExpire terminates an event on, and a missed estimate must never
retire a live outage.

medicalBaselineAffected.description:
Medical-baseline customers in the footprint — people whose medical
equipment depends on grid power. No other feed we carry reports this.

outageId.description: PG&E OUTAGE_ID, the native id half of "pge:{id}"
outageId.title: --- outage (source `pge`) ---

v1RoadIncidentDetail.description:
Kind-specific only. The incident type is the envelope `category`, the human
location is `area_label`, and the short line is the `headline` — none are
repeated here.

duration.title: AI-assessed: unknown | < 1 hour | several hours | ongoing

logNumber.title: CHP log number; for a Caltrans closure, its closure id

metadata.title: structured extras from AI analysis (internal keys stripped)

v1Severity.description: The shipped scale, unchanged. rank = enum value; INFO=0 ... EXTREME=4.

domain.title: fire | evacuation | weather | roads | seismic | power (| comms when enabled)

status.title: worst source_status across the domain's layers

activeEvacuations.description:
NULLABLE: serializes as JSON `null` (not 0) when evacuation data is
UNAVAILABLE. The OpenAPI type is `integer` only because Swagger 2.0 cannot
express a nullable scalar — do NOT coerce null→0 (an error must never become
a 0). null = UNAVAILABLE, 0 = confirmed no active zones, N = active.

areaDesc.title: NWS free-text area (no envelope equivalent for zone alerts)

nwsSeverity.title: raw NWS vocabulary (Extreme..Minor), distinct from unified severity

v1WeatherAlertDetail.title:
Detail messages carry only KIND-SPECIFIC fields not already in the Event
envelope. Fields that duplicate an envelope field are NOT repeated here:
  - the NWS event name is the envelope `category`
  - the sending office is `provenance.source_name`

v1WeatherForecast.description:
WeatherForecast is a location's short-range fire-weather forecast: the raw NWS
gridpoint series (wind/gust/RH/temp) plus an at-a-glance summary. Informational
only — it never implies a fire-weather WARNING (issued products are in
FireWeatherConditions). See docs/design/fire-weather-forecast-design.md.

hasPerimeter.title: true when geometry is a FIRIS perimeter polygon

ingestBearer.description:
A per-reporter token issued by the operators (256-bit random, shown once).
Only its SHA-256 lives server-side. Identity comes from the token alone:
any reporter id in the body is ignored.
